trust_decision.summary: Whether a submitted 6-digit email sign-in code proves control of the mailbox is decided by the next-auth Prisma adapter's useVerificationToken (delete-by-identifier+token, no failed-attempt limit), with codes made by Math.random in the Nodemailer provider config.

landing_point.why: The summary says '6-digit magic-link code' / weak randomness; generateVerificationToken with Math.random is the only visible code generator for sign-in.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The report is about weak randomness; swapping Math.random for crypto.randomInt makes the code 'unpredictable', and attempt limiting looks like next-auth's / the infra rate limiter's job (the app already rate-limits sign-in at nextAuth.ts:97-100), so the adapter and schema look out of scope.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The VerificationToken table is shared: WhatsApp webhook tokens (identifier 'whatsapp webhook', value null) and change-email tokens (identifier '<userId>-changeEmail', value = new email) must not be counted or deleted by the failed-attempt logic; a legitimate user who mistypes the code once must still be able to sign in with the right code; legacy rows with value null must still work.

parallel failed attempts (atomic updateMany increment then deleteMany)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Change-email verification code generated as a short numeric code (same as sign-in), verified at packages/auth/src/api/updateUserEmail.ts:14-28 with no attempt counter.

Lives in a different file (api/) from the adapter.

O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A shared util in another package that a maintainer would reach for; it is a second weak-randomness primitive at distance from the landing point.
